display_name: Glioma MGMT-methylation status from mpMRI radiomics (tabular, classical baseline)

input_contract.population: Adults with pathologically confirmed glioblastoma (UPenn-GBM cohort) with pre-operative structural multiparametric MRI (FLAIR, T1, T1-contrast, T2) and a recorded MGMT promoter methylation status.

quality_constraints.imaging: 1728 CaPTk-computed radiomic summary features (intensity/texture/shape) over the automatic tumor-region segmentation (edema, enhancing tumor, necrotic core) for each of FLAIR/T1/T1GD/T2 — pre-extracted by the UPenn-GBM CaPTk pipeline, not computed by this engine from raw DICOM.

temporal_validation: not applicable — single pre-operative scan per case, no index or outcome time

calibration.note: Production-rigor evaluation (repeats=10, full 256-case dataset, 204 train / 52 test) ran 2026-08-29: best classical balanced accuracy 0.474 (rbf_svc). An architecture sweep (ANOVA vs PCA reduction x 4/6/8 qubit-equivalent components, 4 classical/quantum model families) found every configuration in the 0.44-0.55 balanced-accuracy band, i.e. statistically indistinguishable from chance (0.50). NOT registered as an operational reference: an at-chance classifier is not treated as a usable coverage-closing model.

safety.disclaimer: Research MGMT-methylation status estimate from pre-extracted mpMRI radiomic features, not a glioma diagnosis, grade classification, or tumor segmentation.
limitations: This is an MGMT-promoter-methylation molecular-characterization proxy, NOT tumor segmentation, grade classification, or subtype characterization as the spec's P3 task (glioma lesion characterization on mpMRI) more broadly calls for — the registry's 'glioma-characterization-mpmri' stub remains 'not available' for those parts of the task.

Radiomic features come from CaPTk's automatic tumor-region segmentation, not manually corrected contours or an independently-verified segmentation quality check — errors in that upstream segmentation propagate into these features uncorrected.

All cases are pathology-confirmed glioblastoma (WHO grade IV) from a single academic center (University of Pennsylvania) — no external cohort, no other glioma grades, and no screening-population generalization.

No biomarker-supported evaluation set beyond the cohort's own recorded MGMT status; no approved label policy exists yet — per FR-033 this MUST remain research-only and MUST NOT be described as diagnostic.
No external cohort or site-held-out validation was possible (single-site UPenn release).

PRIMARY FINDING: this classifier does not exceed chance. Production-rigor evaluation (10 repeats, full 256-case cohort) gave balanced accuracy 0.474; a follow-up architecture sweep over ANOVA/PCA reduction x 4/6/8 components found every configuration in [0.44, 0.55], i.e. statistically indistinguishable from a coin flip. This is registered as availability='not available' — it exists only as a documented, honest negative result, not a usable coverage-closing model.

model_card.intended_use: Documents a completed, honestly-negative benchmark of a classical gradient-boosted classifier on CaPTk radiomic features for MGMT promoter methylation status. Not usable for any assessment — see PRIMARY FINDING in safety.limitations.
model_card.excluded_use: Any clinical use. Glioma diagnosis, grading, subtyping, or treatment selection. Any use as evidence of a patient's actual MGMT status. Any live case assessment (model is not available).
model_card.training_population: 256 labeled cases total (UPenn-GBM cohort, pathology-confirmed glioblastoma, definite MGMT status recorded: 148 unmethylated / 108 methylated), split 204 train / 52 test by patient-group holdout.
model_card.evaluation_population: Stratified group-based holdout (by patient) of the same UPenn-GBM radiomics table. No external cohort.
model_card.label_policy: Binary MGMT column from the UPenn-GBM clinical release ('Methylated' vs 'Unmethylated'); rows with 'Not Available' or 'Indeterminate' status excluded.

data_sources.label: UPenn-GBM collection (The Cancer Imaging Archive)
data_sources.citation: Bakas et al., The University of Pennsylvania glioblastoma (UPenn-GBM) cohort: advanced MRI, clinical, genomics, and radiomics. Scientific Data, 2022. DOI: 10.1038/s41597-022-01560-7

model_card.explanation_method: input_sensitivity over the 4 ANOVA-selected radiomic features
